title: 1975 AHSME Problem 22
statement:
If \(p\) and \(q\) are primes and \(x^2-px+q=0\) has distinct positive integral roots, then which of the following statements are true?

I. The difference of the roots is odd.

II. At least one root is prime.

III. \(p^2-q\) is prime.

IV. \(p+q\) is prime.

solutions.text:
The positive integer roots have product \(q,\) so they are \(1\) and \(q.\) Their sum is \(p=q+1,\) which is prime only when \(q=2,\) giving \(p=3\) and roots \(1,2.\) Their difference is \(1,\) one root is prime, \(p^2-q=7,\) and \(p+q=5;\) therefore all four statements hold.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: The product of the two positive integer roots is the prime \(q\)
The roots must be \(1,q,\) and their prime sum forces \(q=2\)
